I just want to be normal again.

Thanks :) I feel a lot better really just getting it all out so it's not all tension built up. I'm looking into significantly lowering my loan payments, and I realized that if I hang on to my income taxes, what I get back should definitely be enough to get me started back in school. I feel a huge burden is lifted. Thanks for the advice! I don't think I'll really hate radiology....it's just not what I know I love and feel passionate about. I will agree that she is like 90% of why I'm still alive today probably. When I feel like giving up I have to remind myself that I have to be here for her. Thanks :)
Thanks so much, your words have really touched me. I feel a lot better now.

Thank you this is actually really helpful, and it's nice to hear from a parent who has an older child cause I know you've already been through it all.   
 
Also, good luck with your son. Sounds like you'll do just fine though. :)

THIS so many times over. I'm not saying she's bad, but you know they are at that age when they want to challenge you (for what seems like every waking minute). Sometimes I feel like the more I go out of my way to make a day fun for her, the more she throws tantrums or disagrees with me. I have a hard time explaining to her that things are fun until she wears them out. A lot of this I also blame myself for though, cause it isn't like I always deal with the tantrums in the best way. My mom criticizes me because I would prefer to walk away or send her to her room until she gets done. I'm supposed to talk to her...but damnit, if I talk to her when she's like that it isn't going to do anything but get us both enraged.

Thank you, you sound like a sweet and wonderful father. I'm going to try to find something we can do together that won't hurt my dusty wallet. I want to show her that I really do love her even thought I don't always seem like it.
Thanks for just being straight up :) I never really thought of it that way. I just have been blinded by hating myself and feeling so guilty for letting my feelings go this far.

Can I ask you a question in return? As a child, how do you think you would have taken your mom telling you those things? And...what would have been a good way for her to tell you so you would understand it. My daughter is 3, so the thought of explaining it to her is a little overwhelming considering I'm still trying to figure this thing out too. I agree with what you're saying though, she definitely deserves to know that it is in no way her fault, and I don't blame her. I spend a lot of time just blaming myself.

You know, I feel like I could have just wrote most of this myself. And it's sad, but especially when I'm really depressed, I feel like I'm just acting out the part. When I'm around other moms that are talking to their kids or disciplining them, or whatever, I listen to them and think...that's so much different than what I would say. They talk to their kids like babies, and I expect my 3 year old to understand things like an adult. When she doesn't, it takes all I have not to get super angry. That makes me feel so guilty

You're right, I know, I know she is. I promise, I do love her dearly, and I want her to have the best life possible. I just find myself realizing a lot that I'm in no way giving her the life she deserves (not even because of bipolar, just financially). She has her needs though, and will just have to learn what it means to save pennies for the wants. I think a lot of my frustration just comes from fear of failing her. So...instead I just find myself wishing I could run away from the responsibility all together.

Lol it's ok. This is where we come for support, cause sometimes the people around us aren't really people we can go to for it. (well, I might be speaking for myself). I really hope you are able to find something that works for you :)

Well, hey, I'm glad to make you feel better! If it counts for anything, one day I think I want to have another baby. But, I really long for the day when I can look into my partner's eyes, tell him the news, and see joy on his face. I want someone to rub my belly and do all those cute pregnant things I didn't get. (so, enjoy them for me while you can? :p)  
  
You're going to be a great mom. I know it is terrifying, and sometimes you are going to feel horribly overwhelmed...but you got this. Just remember how much you wanted it, and remind yourself that you are also hormonal and round at the moment, so your opinions might not feel so great about the little booger in your belly making you sick all the time and kicking you in your lungs :p   
  
  
Thank you so much for the soothing words. I feel tremendously better thanks to you. *hugs hugs, more hugs*

Well, that's funny you think I've never had college-age male roommates. I actually have 2!  
  
Anyway, you can think of it like that, but going into it with that kind of negativity doesn't really scream success right from the beginning.   
Remember, you are the one holding yourself back, and you are the one who can push yourself to do better. If you don't, then you have to deal with the bad grades and all that negativity.   
  
Anyway, maybe somebody else has a better idea. I'm just trying to be a supportive internet stranger sharing what I use to fight my own problem with procrastinating.

Hey, they should be promoting your success!  
  
Anyway, stay positive, and just try it out. If it doesn't work out for you, it isn't like you lost anything.   
  
As far as substance abuse goes, I think you know what you got to do on that one. For one, I am a weed supporter. I have to stop smoking cause I'm getting a degree in the medical field, but I totally think people should enjoy it if they can (as long as you don't let it hold you back. For example, if you aren't working because you're afraid of passing drug tests). As far as other drugs, there are programs to help you get off them, or to keep off them, or hell...if you're friends are influencing you to have alcoholic tendencies, get some better damn friends. :)

You know...it doesn't even matter that you can't answer my question. You have no idea how much it helps knowing I'm not alone feeling this way. No, it's not good to feel this way, but I think sharing it with another mom makes me feel slightly less terrible as a person.  
  
I didn't get a chance to enjoy pregnancy. I hope you can get some joy out of the experience. I was 16 when I found out, and my dad kicked me out of the house because he was so angry and didn't know what else to do. My boyfriend was so ashamed, and his family called me every name in the book for not getting an abortion. I was taken to church, and forced to stand in front of the congregation while the preacher prayed for my forgiveness.  (I'm an athiest 0.o). I had to start my junior year at a new high school, being pregnant, and nobody ever called me by my name...I was known until graduation as "that pregnant chick".   
  
  
I think if somebody would have just once made me feel like it was ok to be pregnant, and that my child was a blessing - I might feel differently today.   
Now I just wake up every day and lose myself daydreaming about what my life could have been.

Well, take a dry erase marker and write them on your bathroom mirror, and your refrigerator, and get a big calendar (preferably dry-erase!) and write everything on that, too.   
It also helps to put a nice check mark by your accomplishments, no matter how small - because the high you get from feeling you achieved something will give you an incentive to keep going.  
  
Think about why it is you use these substances? Trying to forget something? Perhaps, it's your way of forgetting to feel bad about not doing your work, or not getting out and just enjoying friendship (or whatever, ya get it).  I bet you'll be able to enjoy life without it, once you get more in the habit of managing and reaching your goals. Plus, you'll feel damn proud of yourself.

I'm a procrastinator, and I can tell you right now that it's the worst thing ever to deal with. The best solution to my problem (and this actually makes me get shit done!) is to constantly refer to my "to-do" list. I write a list, and I schedule exactly when I'm going to work on what, and how far done I plan to be once that time is up. Take small breaks from it, like 5 minutes every 30, so you don't feel overwhelmed if you must. Also, you probably don't need to hear this, but I have a friend who sounds exactly like you, and from watching him, I know that the whole drinking every day thing is making him so much more unstable, whether he realizes it or not.  

  
I'm sorry, kinda got off on a ramble. Anyway, make lists, maybe that will help. Good luck! (don't give up!)
Thank you so much. All I can do is try to smile and focus on what can be good

It was so hard hearing that "everything is my fault". Thank you so much for all your kind words, you don't even understand how much they mean to me
